_meta.purpose: Proves Issue-14 BIRD-evaluator alignment: where our default comparator matches the official BIRD evaluator (set(predicted) == set(ground_truth)) and — crucially — where it deliberately diverges. Each divergence is pinned as a PAIR of triples on the same data: one under BIRD_RULES (the 'set' rule, reproducing BIRD's verdict) and one under DEFAULT_RULES (our stricter / more lenient verdict). 'BIRD-aligned' is thus proven by the fixture, not asserted. Full audit + rationale: docs/eval/comparator-rule-set.md.
_meta.format: Each case: {id, description, gold_sql, gold_result:{columns,rows}, candidate_result:{columns,rows}, expected_verdict, rules?:[...]}. Cases with 'rules':['column_position','set','exact'] reproduce BIRD's set-comparison; cases without 'rules' use eval.compare.DEFAULT_RULES (our default). Loaded automatically by tests/test_compare.py.
_meta.bird_reference: set(predicted_res) == set(ground_truth_res) over cursor.fetchall(), from AlibabaResearch/DAMO-ConvAI bird/llm/src/evaluation.py — order-insensitive, duplicate-collapsing, no float tolerance.

cases.description: Gold keeps duplicate rows, candidate collapsed them (COUNT vs COUNT DISTINCT). Under BIRD's set() the duplicate is dropped on both sides, so the multiplicity loss is invisible → BIRD says correct.
Same data under our DEFAULT_RULES (multiset, no de-dup): the row-multiplicity difference is a real error → incorrect. This is the BIRD blind spot we deliberately close.
Gold declares a top-level ORDER BY but candidate returns the same rows in the wrong order. BIRD's set() is order-agnostic even here, so it cannot see the broken ORDER BY → BIRD says correct.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT name FROM merchants ORDER BY name;

cases.description: Same data under DEFAULT_RULES: order_insensitive sees the gold's top-level ORDER BY and treats row order as the answer, so the reordered candidate is incorrect. We catch the broken ORDER BY BIRD masks.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT name FROM merchants ORDER BY name;

cases.description: An AVG differing only in the 9th decimal. BIRD compares floats exactly (no tolerance), so identical-to-9-digits values are judged different → BIRD says incorrect. A false negative on an equally-correct query.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT avg(amount) AS avg_amount FROM payments;

cases.description: Same data under DEFAULT_RULES: float_tolerance rounds to 6 decimals, so insignificant precision noise compares equal → correct. We forgive the FP noise BIRD penalizes (the one axis where we are more lenient than BIRD).
cases.gold_sql: SELECT avg(amount) AS avg_amount FROM payments;

cases.description: Both sides return NULL in the same position. BIRD compares raw None in the set and matches; our null_sentinel reaches the same verdict → aligned, correct.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT phone FROM users WHERE id = 5;

cases.description: Gold NULL vs candidate 0. Under BIRD's set(), None and 0 are distinct elements → incorrect; our sentinel agrees → aligned.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT balance FROM accounts WHERE id = 9;

cases.description: Two empty result sets: set() == set() → BIRD correct; we agree (both-empty is the correct-able empty case) → aligned.
Empty gold vs non-empty candidate: set() != set({(1,)}) → BIRD incorrect; we agree (empty is never auto-correct) → aligned.
Same value under a renamed column label. BIRD's fetchall() tuples carry no labels, so it matches positionally; column_position names that same contract → aligned, correct.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT name AS customer FROM customers WHERE id = 1;
